**The meaning of the verse**
﴿أَوْ كَالَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحْيِي هَٰذِهِ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا ۖ فَأَمَاتَهُ اللَّهُ مِائَةَ عَامٍ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ ۖ قَالَ كَمْ لَبِثْتَ ۖ قَالَ لَبِثْتُ يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ ۖ قَالَ بَل لَّبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عَامٍ فَانظُرْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ ۖ وَانظُرْ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِّلنَّاسِ ۖ وَانظُرْ إِلَى الْعِظَامِ كَيْفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْسُوهَا لَحْمًا ۚ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ قَالَ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

Or have you seen, O Messenger, the like of the one who passed by a town whose houses had collapsed and fallen in on their roofs, and he said: "How will Allah bring this town to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then returned his soul to him and said to him: "How long did you remain dead?" He said: "I remained a day or part of a day." So He told him that he had remained dead for a hundred years, and commanded him to look at his food and drink, and how Allah had kept them from changing for this long time. And He commanded him to look at his donkey, how Allah brought it to life after it had been scattered bones, and said to him: "And so that We may make you a sign for people," that is, a clear proof of Allah's power to resurrect after death. And He commanded him to look at the bones, how Allah raises some of them onto others and joins them together, then, once they are joined, clothes them with flesh, then brings life back into them. When this became clear to him with his own eyes, he acknowledged Allah's greatness, and that He has power over all things, and he became a sign for people.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did the man say to himself when he saw the ruined town? And was he denying Allah's power? (No, he was amazed and wanted to see how bringing back to life happens; asking in order to understand is not wrong.)
2. How long did the man think he had stayed? And how long did he really stay? And in which things did Allah show him the answer?
3. What did the man say at the end of the story? And how does what he saw show us that Allah will bring all people back to life on the Day of Resurrection?

**This week's exercise**
Plant a dry seed together (a bean or a lentil) in wet cotton wool, and watch it every day: how does green life come out of the dead seed? At the end of the week, your child tells you the story in their own words and ends it with the man's words: "I know that Allah has power over all things."
